answer: Reputation-weighted rate limiting. Each identity starts on a low throughput ridge, and sustained useful activity raises its quota along a smooth terrace while idle or disputed accounts slide back down. The system reads behavioral consistency as a signal, so fresh identities face severe per-request delays and capped concurrency that only genuine long-run participation relaxes. An attacker must run many identities through that slow climb, paying orchestration, monitoring, and wasted compute on each for weeks before the quota curve bends.
